messages.subject: NIMBLE user defined distribution registration
parts:
I have to design a complicate density function in my algorithm with large amount of mixture components. I can define a "d" function as my user defined function, but the "d" function sometimes returns the "-Inf" and thus I can not define the "r" function to generate the random number from this density. 

Is there any possible solution that one can define a density function without defining the "r" function?  Particularly when. the density is possible to return an "-Inf" value. 

Many thanks.

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: NIMBLE user defined distribution registration
parts:
Thanks for the question.

This should be possible.  I assume you mean you have written the d function so it sometimes correctly returns -Inf for the log probability (density), i.e. when the inputs have probability 0.

The r function should generate a random draw from the distribution.  By definition it should never return a value for which the d function returns log probability -Inf, since such a value has no chance of occurring.

If the r function is not needed by an algorithm such as MCMC, you do not need to provide it.  In that case you should see a message that nimble is creating a proxy r function for you.  The "proxy" means nimble has created a do-nothing version of an R function.  If you provide initial values for the nodes in question and they are not posterior predictive nodes, then MCMC will not actually call the r function.  If you are using another method such as SMC, then yes you will need the r function.

I am not sure I have got the gist of your question.  Please follow up with more details if you are still stuck.

-Perry

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: NIMBLE user defined distribution registration
parts:
Hi

In general, you don't need to call the d function from within the r function. 

Assuming that you are able to simulate from each of your mixture components, you should be able to write an r function that  
1) chooses a mixture component at random, given the set of mixture weights 
2) samples the corresponding distribution 
3) returns the result of step 2. 

Below is a script with a toy example - hope it helps. 

Best regards
David

library(nimble)

dMixGamma <- nimbleFunction (
  run = function(x       = double(0),
                 shape   = double(1, default=1.0),
                 scale   = double(1, default=1.0),
                 weights = double(1),
                 log     = integer(0, default=0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    nComponents = length(weights)
    # Ensure weights are normalised
    probs = nimNumeric(length=nComponents)
    for (ii in 1:nComponents)
      probs[ii] = weights[ii] / sum(weights[])
    # Mixture log-likelihood
    likelihood = 0
    for (ii in 1:nComponents)
      likelihood = likelihood + probs[ii] * dgamma(x, shape=shape[ii], scale=scale[ii], log=FALSE)
    if (log)
      return(log(likelihood))
    return(likelihood)
  }
)


rMixGamma <- nimbleFunction (
  run = function(n       = integer(0, default=1),
                 shape   = double(1, default=1.0),
                 scale   = double(1, default=1.0),
                 weights = double(1)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    nComponents = length(weights)
    # Ensure weights are normalised
    probs = nimNumeric(length=nComponents)
    for (ii in 1:nComponents)
      probs[ii] = weights[ii] / sum(weights[])
    # Step 1: sample a mixture component
    ii = rcat(1, probs[1:nComponents])
    # Step 2: sample iith distribution in the mixture component
    x = rgamma(1, shape=shape[ii], scale=scale[ii])
    # Step 3: return x
    return(x)
  }
)


registerDistributions(list(dMixGamma = list(
  BUGSdist = "dMixGamma(shape, scale)",
  discrete = FALSE,
  types    = c("value=double(0)"),
  pqAvail  = FALSE)))


c_dMixGamma = compileNimble(dMixGamma)
c_rMixGamma = compileNimble(rMixGamma)

## Test
Shape = c(0.1, 1, 5)
Scale = c(1, 1, 2)
Weights = c(3, 1, 13)

y = replicate(1E5, c_rMixGamma(1, shape = Shape, scale = Scale, weights = Weights))

x  = seq(0, max(y), l=10001)
dx = sapply(x, "c_dMixGamma", shape = Shape, scale = Scale, weights = Weights)

hist(y, n=101, freq=FALSE)
lines(dx~x, col="red", lwd=3)
